GOOD TO KNOW

Emails are no longer timed against the reply times written for web chat. Without changing a policy, an email's reply is due within the policy's answer time for email, a WhatsApp message within WhatsApp's and an SMS within SMS's; web chat keeps the policy's own reply times. Reply times run on the clock, not on opening hours.

An alert for a late reply is sent once for each waiting customer message. A note or an automatic message on the same conversation no longer sends it again.

The ticket import reads from HoduCC and never changes anything there. It brings in open tickets only. Chat, WhatsApp and SMS transcripts and attachments cannot be brought in: HoduCC does not give them out.

FOR AGENTS

Your callbacks: a callback in My work can now be opened. It says where it stands, and has Mark as done (with a note) and Cancel it. A callback closes by itself once its call has been made and wrapped up, whoever made the call; callbacks that were left "in progress" after their call are cleared automatically.

A personal callback is kept for you for 30 minutes after it falls due; after that any qualified colleague may take it. The desk now says so.

On WhatsApp, SMS and social conversations the desk says "conversation" where it said "chat", and the reply timer shows hours.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Late reply alerts name what is waiting: "An email from … is waiting too long for a reply", with the subject, the queue, the agent it is with, the time allowed and how long overdue. The same for WhatsApp, SMS, web chat and social messages.

The floor's callbacks panel lists callbacks in progress and has Mark as done.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Reply times for each channel: on Service levels a policy can set "First reply within" and "Each later reply within" per channel, beside the answer times per channel. Left empty, email, WhatsApp, SMS and social use their channel's answer time, and web chat the policy's reply times. The list shows the times that apply, in words.

Import tickets from HoduCC: Tickets → Import → From HoduCC. Enter the address, token and tenant ID, map statuses, queues, agents and customer fields, run a dry run to see what would come in, then import. Each ticket gets a new number and keeps its old one, which can be searched; its opened and updated times, comments at their own times, and every original field are kept. Customers are matched by phone or email, otherwise created; an existing customer only has gaps filled. Where the mailbox an email thread came to is connected, the original emails are read from it; a customer's reply to the old thread, or one quoting the old number, lands on the imported ticket. Call history is attached to call tickets, and recordings are copied only when asked. Running it again adds only what is new. Undo puts away the untouched tickets of a run for 30 days without deleting anything. The import sends no notices, routes nothing and starts no surveys, and imported tickets are counted apart from tickets opened here.

The ticket report has an Imported column."}
